wording: For the frequency-dependent Moran process under weak selection (N w << 1), a single A mutant has fixation probability above 1/N if and only if (N - 2)a + (2N - 1)b > (N + 1)c + (2N - 4)d (Nowak et al. 2004, restated in P58), which for large N becomes a + 2b > c + 2d, the one-third law. P58 explains the 1/3 by sojourn times: along an invasion path a player meets B-players twice as often as A-players. Outside weak selection the minimum basin of attraction a mutant needs goes from 2/3 (N w << 1) towards 1 (large N w), so strong selection makes invasion harder.
